newsitem.title: FRANCE: Car sales in France up 89 pct in Sept first half.
newsitem.headline: Car sales in France up 89 pct in Sept first half.

text.p: New car sales in France were around 89-percent higher in the first 15 days of September from year-ago levels, the chairman of the CNPA, the national council of automotive professions, said on Thursday.
Sales are up sharply ahead of the expiry on September 30 of a year-long new-cars-for-old state rebate programme.
Sales were weak last year as a prior programme had expired on June 30, 1995, and incentives were not reintroduced until last October to support the French car market.
Car sales totalled 116,585 last September, compared with an average for the month of 150,000 to 170,000, CNPA Chairman Jean-Pierre Henaut told reporters.
An industry source said sales this month were expected to reach around 200,000, a year-over-year increase of more than 70 percent.

Henaut said he expected 1996 car sales in France to exceed two million units, making it the best year for the industry since 1992. But he said the market could plunge to between 1.5 million and 1.6 million units in 1997 if the rebate programme was not extended.
Henaut's 1997 estimate is among the more pessimistic.
Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer this week said he estimated the core market, excluding sales driven by special incentives, at around 1.9 million units.
